note: Test keys, derived from the issuer's name. Never credentials. A case names the model it is read under in `model`.

cases.name: authority restored at the source (holdings)
cases.about: The operator withdraws the orchestrator's mandate and later gives it the same again. The orchestrator passes nothing on anew. Where a delegation holds while its issuer holds, the agent has its mandate back. Where a delegation is bound to the grant it was passed on under, it has not: that grant is gone.

statements.reason: the orchestrator passes air on to the agent

cases.name: authority widened at the source (holdings)
cases.about: The orchestrator holds air and passes on air and rotation. Later the operator gives the orchestrator rotation too. Where a delegation holds while its issuer holds, the agent then holds rotation. Where it is bound to its grant, a delegation that listed more than its grant gives nothing, before or after.

statements.reason: the orchestrator passes on more than it holds

cases.name: the same mandate given again (holdings)
cases.about: The operator replaces the orchestrator's mandate with one that lists the same. Where a delegation is bound to its grant this too ends what was passed on, because the grant it was passed on under has been replaced.

statements.reason: the orchestrator passes air on to the agent

cases.name: the same mandate given again (grant_bound)

statements.reason: the orchestrator passes air on to the agent

cases.name: passed on before anything was held (holdings)
cases.about: The orchestrator passes air on before it is given air. Until it is given air, nothing is established for it, and so nothing for the agent. Afterwards, where a delegation holds while its issuer holds, the agent holds air. Where it is bound to a grant, there was no grant to bind it to.

statements.reason: passed on before the orchestrator held anything

cases.about: A delegation issued at the same instant as its grant is under that grant.

statements.reason: passed on at the instant it was given

cases.name: two links, and the first grant is replaced (holdings)
cases.about: The mandate goes through two orchestrators to the agent. The operator replaces the first orchestrator's mandate with one that lists the same. Where delegations are bound to their grants, the second orchestrator's is no longer under the first's grant, and so nothing below it holds either.

statements.reason: the orchestrator passes air on to a second
the second passes it on to the agent
